answer: Picture the agent economy as a busy wharf where every newcomer must dock in plain sight. Each epoch an agent must gather fresh attestations from a quota of distinct, already-established counterparties, and the trust graph is audited for clustering, like a vine choking one terrace. A sybil ring that mostly attests itself collapses to near-zero diversity and is flagged. To fake N identities an attacker must buy genuine interactions from N separate honest agents, each charging a fee, so cost climbs at least linearly in N and worse as honest partners grow scarce.
